top_choice_rationale: P003 (Helpman and Melitz) is the achievement I judge strongest on originality, maturity, attribution and citation scope. Melitz (2003), together with the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple work on exporting versus FDI, moved trade analysis from the industry to the firm. It added a selection and reallocation margin with its own testable predictions, which firm-level data from many countries have tested for more than twenty years. The two-name attribution is clean, and the citation can be limited to the selection model, leaving out the exporter facts (Bernard and Jensen) and the parallel quantitative route (Eaton and Kortum). The main costs are the omission of those contributors, the Pareto-dependence of the size of the welfare gains, and the risk that the committee sees this as continuing the 2008 trade prize. I think the unit of analysis differs, so I do not count the 2008 prize as decisive. P001 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) is a close second. Its originating-ideas attribution is defensible and its policy reach is greater, but it leaves out the Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets group, it raises priority questions involving Fischer and Phelps, and the micro evidence on state-dependent pricing weakens the Calvo device as a description. P002 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley) is a conceptually strong framework with clean credit, but its cross-country identification is weaker and it neighbours the 2024 institutions prize. P000 is last because P001 to P003 are all mature, substantive achievements that could support an award. I did not weigh the opening or round-2 support counts as merit.
recusal_note: Disclosed, not adjudicated. My research on firm dynamics, reallocation and misallocation is close in subject to P003 (B021), which I rank first, so I rely on the common criteria and the stated uncertainties. I have no documented tie to Helpman or Melitz, nor to Calvo, Taylor or Woodford. I am a frequent co-author of, and IIES colleague to, committee members Krusell and Hassler, who are not candidates. I am also an IIES colleague of Torsten Persson (P002) and a long-running co-author of Peter Klenow (B050, not in any proposal).
